codeQualityIssues.description: In stage-loop-factory.ts, the scrutiny phase detection uses string prefix matching (`phase.title.startsWith("Scrutiny: ")`) which couples the prompt builder to the exact title format set in milestone-tracker.ts. A shared constant for the prefix would be more maintainable, but this matches the existing pattern used for "Validation: " detection in the same file, so it's consistent.

The test for 'only includes configured commands in hard gates' (line ~294) asserts `prompt.toContain("npm test")` but doesn't assert that the unconfigured commands (typecheck, lint) are NOT present in the hard gate sections. It only has a comment saying 'typecheck and lint should be noted as not configured, not as hard gates' without verification. The assertion is incomplete but not blocking since the 'uses exact command strings from config' test covers the inverse more thoroughly.

The CommandsSchema in loader.ts does not apply the `noShellMetachars` validator used for `project_cwd`. Since these command strings will be executed by the worker process (not by Flywheel itself), this is not a direct security risk, but adding the same shell metacharacter guard would be a defense-in-depth measure. This is a design choice, not a bug.

codeReview.summary: Well-structured implementation of the scrutiny validation phase. The code is clean, well-documented, and follows existing codebase conventions. The config schema extension is additive (optional field), maintaining backward compatibility. The prompt template is comprehensive with clear hard gate instructions, per-phase review sections, and synthesis guidance. The wiring in stage-loop-factory.ts correctly detects scrutiny phases by title prefix and constructs the appropriate context from available phase data. All 24 tests pass covering config schema, prompt content, missing commands, per-phase review, and config-driven commands.

issues.description: String literal 'Scrutiny: ' is used for prefix matching in both stage-loop-factory.ts and execution-loop.ts (line 1066). Consider extracting to a shared constant alongside the existing pattern. However, this is consistent with how 'Validation: ' prefix is handled in the same codebase.

Test 'only includes configured commands in hard gates' has a comment about checking unconfigured commands aren't in hard gates but no actual assertion for it. Consider adding expect(prompt).not.toContain('bunx tsc') or similar to make the test more robust.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The project's AGENTS.md configuration table (flywheel.toml fields) does not yet document the new `commands` section (test, typecheck, lint) or the `skip_scrutiny` config flag that were added. Future workers won't know about these config options unless they read the schema directly. The AGENTS.md should be updated to include these new config fields.

The .factory/services.yaml already has a `commands` section with `test: bun test` and `typecheck: bunx tsc --noEmit` but no `lint` entry. This is separate from the flywheel.toml `commands` section but serves a similar purpose. No action needed — these are different systems (Factory vs Flywheel config), but worth noting the parallel.

summary: PASS. The scrutiny-validation-phase feature is well-implemented with clean code, comprehensive test coverage (24 tests), and proper integration. It correctly adds a `commands` config section to flywheel.toml schema, creates a scrutiny prompt template that reads commands from config (not hardcoded), warns when commands are missing without failing, treats configured commands as hard gates, and instructs per-phase code review. The wiring in stage-loop-factory.ts properly detects scrutiny phases and constructs the appropriate prompt context. All three validation contract assertions (VAL-EXEC-003, VAL-EXEC-004, VAL-EXEC-011) have dedicated test coverage. Only minor non-blocking observations: string prefix matching could use shared constants, one test has incomplete assertions, and command strings lack shell metacharacter validation.
